sources.title: Boost — shared ownership versus thread safety
sources.version_or_date: Boost 1.55.0, page explicitly says released in 2013
sources.sections_read: Boost 1.55 shared_ptr introduction and Thread Safety
sources.confirmed: The versioned documentation distinguishes shared ownership from the conditions under which shared_ptr objects may be used concurrently.
sources.limits: A shared_ptr is an owning handle rather than a Rust borrow; its documented handle operations do not make every access to its pointee safe. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C22.json.

sources.title: Concurrent Ruby — thread safety separate from mutability
sources.confirmed: Concurrent Ruby documents thread safety as a separate property and distinguishes the safety of its abstractions from the safety of contained mutable objects.
sources.limits: Ruby's library guarantees are per abstraction and do not automatically cover referenced mutable payloads; this is a vocabulary precedent, not a transferable Rust trait definition. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C22.json.

sources.title: Qt — thread-safe versus reentrant
sources.version_or_date: Qt 6.12 live documentation; no publication timestamp established
sources.sections_read: Definitions of thread-safe and reentrant; Counter examples
sources.confirmed: Qt distinguishes using different instances concurrently from using the same instance concurrently; its mutable mutex example also separates const access from physical immutability.
sources.limits: Qt's definition covers class operations generally; Rust's trait should remain specifically about safe concurrent access through shared references, without promising unrestricted mutation or requiring locks. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C22.json.

sources.title: Clang Thread Safety Analysis — access capabilities and safety contracts
sources.sections_read: Introduction; Basic Concepts: Capabilities; GUARDED_BY and PT_GUARDED_BY; shared/exclusive capability attributes
sources.confirmed: Clang distinguishes shared or exclusive access modes from the concurrency-protection contract and states that annotation terminology was generalized from lock-centric names to capabilities.
sources.limits: These are annotation-based access requirements, not a universal marker for values safely shared through a Rust reference; the mechanism must not replace the trait's existing semantic property. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C22.json.
